verdict.rationale: Temporal documents Schedules that start Workflow Executions at specific times as a more flexible replacement for its Cron Jobs, and a community user describes them as like cron but more flexible, so recurring cron-style scheduling is clearly delivered. Timezone control is not documented; the only time-zone reference is a phase-offset example at 5pm UTC. missing for 10: documented timezone selection for schedules, cron expression syntax details, independent hands-on corroboration of timezone behavior.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can run workflows on cron-style schedules with timezone control

citations.quote: A Schedule contains instructions for starting a Workflow Execution at specific times.
Use a phase offset when you need your recurring Schedule to fire at a specific, human-meaningful time like every 10 days at 5pm UTC on a particular date
Schedules provide a more flexible and user-friendly approach than Temporal Cron Jobs.
For scheduling, there's a Schedules feature that allows you to periodically start a workflow, like a cron but more flexible.
